findings.title: Retry cleanup deletes every WorkflowReminder, not just failed SMS
findings.body: The new deleteMany OR branch matches retryCount > 1 with no method, scheduled: false, or scheduledDate constraint. WorkflowReminder is shared by EMAIL, SMS, and WHATSAPP, and this job runs as the SMS cron. Any non-SMS row that reaches retryCount > 1 (or an SMS row that is already scheduled: true with a Twilio referenceId) is deleted on the next run. That drops the record used to track or cancel the provider message, and it does not match the PR intent of deleting only SMS reminders that failed to schedule twice.

findings.title: Missing phone or empty body never counts as a failed attempt
findings.body: retryCount is only incremented when twilio.scheduleSMS returns a falsy value or throws. If sendTo is missing/empty or the rendered message is empty, the reminder is skipped with scheduled left false and retryCount unchanged. Those rows stay in the unscheduled query and are retried on every cron until scheduledDate is in the past, which is the infinite reschedule this PR is meant to stop (including invalid or absent phone numbers that never reach Twilio).

findings.title: Retry update inside catch can abort the rest of the batch
findings.body: The new workflowReminder.update in the catch is not itself guarded. If that update throws (row already removed by a concurrent cron's deleteMany, or a transient DB error), the exception leaves the catch and the handler stops. Reminders later in unscheduledReminders are never scheduled, and the route fails instead of logging and continuing, which is what the catch did before.

findings.title: retryCount is a lost-update read-modify-write
findings.body: Both failure paths set retryCount to the value loaded at the start of the request (reminder.retryCount + 1) instead of an atomic increment. Overlapping cron runs can both read 0 and both write 1, so the gt: 1 deletion never triggers and failed SMS reminders keep being rescheduled. Use an atomic increment so concurrent failures still reach the retry limit.

findings.title: No test covers retry limit or the widened delete
findings.body: The cron now deletes reminders by retryCount and mutates retryCount on Twilio failure, but nothing asserts that two failures delete only the failed unscheduled SMS row, that a successful schedule is kept, or that EMAIL/WHATSAPP rows are untouched. That deletion is easy to get wrong (the OR is already unscoped) and will not be caught before production.
